Yes, it is price fixing. But, they aren't actively colluding. They are using price signalling to collude. Like airlines, soft drinks, credit cards, snack foods, etc. One raises the price, and the other does too, signalling they are willing to go along with the collusion. They never talk to each other, so it is difficult to prove collusion.

Prices in our economy are not competitive anymore because of this. One of the few exceptions is food supermarkets.
